1	# rf/ — EM simulation workstream
2	
3	Determines whether an antenna placement candidate works, by actually
4	running an FDTD solve (openEMS) on an IFA-over-ground-plane geometry and
5	reporting S11 / resonance / bandwidth / gain / efficiency. One entry point:
6	
7	```python
8	from rf import run_simulation
9	result = run_simulation(config)  # dict in -> dict out, see contract below
10	```
11	
12	No server code lives here — a FastAPI backend (built separately) is meant
13	to import `run_simulation` directly. For the *why* behind every decision
14	below (antenna type, band, solver choice, bugs found and fixed, open
15	questions) see **`progress_simulation.md`** — this file is just the map.
16	
17	## Quickstart
18	
19	```sh
20	# from the repo root
21	rf/.venv/Scripts/python -m rf.run_simulation
22	```
23	
24	Runs a demo GPS-L1 IFA candidate end-to-end (~2 min) and prints the
25	`SimResult` JSON. First time, set up the venvs per "Setup" below.
26	
27	## Module layout
28	
29	```
30	rf/
31	├── __init__.py         # `from rf import run_simulation`
32	├── models.py            # Candidate, Band, SimOptions, SimResult, FDTDStructure, IFA_* constants
33	├── device.py             # load_device() — reads blend_loader-produced device.json
34	├── geometry.py            # build_ifa_geometry() — CSXCAD/openEMS structure for one candidate
35	├── solve.py                # run_fdtd() — runs the solve, CalcPort over the band
36	├── postprocess.py           # postprocess() — port data -> SimResult metrics
37	├── visualize.py               # render_field_animation() / render_s11_plot() — human-facing, opt-in
38	├── run_simulation.py           # run_simulation() orchestrator + __main__ CLI demo
39	├── openems_env.py               # DLL-path setup openEMS/CSXCAD need on Windows before import
40	├── requirements.txt              # numpy/h5py/matplotlib/cython + vendored openEMS/CSXCAD wheels
41	├── vendor/                        # gitignored — vendored openEMS build (~150MB, see Setup)
42	├── .venv/                          # gitignored — openEMS venv
43	└── blend_loader/                    # separate tool + venv: .blend -> device.json (has bpy)
44	    ├── load_blend.py
45	    ├── requirements.txt              # bpy
46	    ├── .venv/                         # gitignored
47	    └── out/                            # generated device.json + STLs, gitignored
48	```
49	
50	All modules use relative imports (`from .models import ...`), so invocation
51	is **always `python -m rf.<module>`**, never `python rf/<module>.py`.
52	
53	## Setup
54	
55	```sh
56	# openEMS venv
57	py -3.11 -m venv rf/.venv
58	mkdir -p rf/vendor
59	curl -L -o rf/vendor/openEMS_v0.0.36.zip \
60	  https://github.com/thliebig/openEMS-Project/releases/download/v0.0.36/openEMS_v0.0.36.zip
61	unzip -q -o rf/vendor/openEMS_v0.0.36.zip -d rf/vendor/
62	cd rf && .venv/Scripts/pip install -r requirements.txt   # cwd matters: wheel paths are relative to this file
63	cd .. && rf/.venv/Scripts/python -m rf.openems_env       # smoke test: imports CSXCAD + openEMS
64	
65	# blend_loader venv (separate — needs bpy, not openEMS)
66	py -3.11 -m venv rf/blend_loader/.venv
67	rf/blend_loader/.venv/Scripts/pip install -r rf/blend_loader/requirements.txt
68	```
69	
70	## Config / result contract
71	
72	Mirrors `frontend/src/lib/types.ts` (snake_case), so a `run_simulation`
73	output can drop straight into `frontend/src/lib/runner.ts` in place of the
74	mock `simulate()`:
75	
76	```jsonc
77	// in
78	{
79	  "candidate": {"candidate_id": "c001", "antenna_type": "IFA",
80	                "position_mm": [5,35,4], "feed_point_mm": [5,33,4],
81	                "length_mm": 26, "orientation": "edge"},
82	  "band": {"id": "gps_l1", "f_low_ghz": 1.565, "f_high_ghz": 1.585,
83	           "s11_db_max": -8, "efficiency_min": 0.45},
84	  "device": { ... },  // types.ts DeviceSpec; board/enclosure/components
85	  "sim": {"mesh_res": "coarse", "boundary": "MUR", "freq_points": 21,
86	          "dump_fields": false}  // see Visualizing below
87	}
88	```
89	
90	```jsonc
91	// out — matches types.ts SimResult exactly
92	{
93	  "candidate_id": "c001", "status": "complete", "runtime_s": 240,
94	  "s11_curve": [{"f_ghz": 1.565, "s11_db": -3.1}, ...],
95	  "s11_min_db": -12.4, "resonant_ghz": 1.5754, "bandwidth_mhz": 18,
96	  "efficiency": 0.52, "peak_gain_dbi": 1.8, "vswr": 1.65,
97	  "sar_w_per_kg": 0.0, "meets_requirements": true, "notes": "..."
98	}
99	```
100	
101	## Visualizing a run
102	
103	`SimOptions.dump_fields=True` (off by default — adds solver overhead and
104	disk I/O) makes `geometry.py` write a time-domain E-field dump, and
105	`run_simulation()` renders it to a GIF, adding `field_animation_path` to
106	the result dict:
107	
108	```python
109	config["sim"]["dump_fields"] = True
110	result = run_simulation(config)
111	result["field_animation_path"]  # GIF of |E| spreading out from the feed
112	```
113	
114	`visualize.render_s11_plot(s11_curve, band, out_png)` turns any
115	`postprocess()` output into a return-loss PNG (threshold + target band
116	marked) — called separately, not gated by `dump_fields`, see the
117	`__main__` block in `run_simulation.py` for the usage pattern.
118	
119	## Real device materials
120	
121	If `config["device"]["manifest_path"]` (or an inline `device["parts"]`)
122	points at a `device.json` from `rf/blend_loader/load_blend.py`,
123	`geometry._add_device_materials()` adds one real CSXCAD dielectric/
124	lossy-metal material per distinct `material_key`, one box per part —
125	automatic, no `SimOptions` flag needed. It's a **bbox-only**
126	approximation (not the actual STL mesh shape — importing ~200 real part
127	meshes as polyhedra would blow the runtime budget) and has **no
128	collision-awareness** with the antenna itself (placement/keepout is on
129	the caller). Ran end-to-end against `data/apple_iphone_15_pro/` (191
130	parts) — see `progress_simulation.md` step 6 for the result and both
131	caveats in detail.
132	
133	## Status
134	
135	Pipeline runs end-to-end (geometry + real device materials → FDTD solve →
136	S11/VSWR/gain/efficiency → optional field GIF), but **the IFA is not yet
137	cross-checked against a known-good result** — resonance/dimensions are a
138	first guess, not tuned or validated. See `progress_simulation.md` →
139	"Steps" for exactly what's done, what bugs were found and fixed, and
140	what's still open (tutorial cross-check, PyNEC cross-check).

208	   `build_ifa_geometry()` in `rf/geometry.py`: ground plane + short pin +
209	   radiating arm as CSXCAD PEC boxes, fed by an `AddLumpedPort`, no

213	5. ~~Wrap end-to-end as `run_simulation(config) -> result dict`~~ **Done**
214	   — `rf/solve.py`'s `run_fdtd()` + `rf/postprocess.py`'s `postprocess()`
215	   also implemented (S11 curve, resonance,
216	   bandwidth, VSWR from `CalcPort`; gain/efficiency from `CalcNF2FF` vs.
217	   `port.P_acc`; SAR still stubbed `0.0`, no tissue phantom yet). **Ran
218	   end-to-end against the GPS-L1 demo candidate and it produced a complete
219	   result** — but getting it running surfaced three real bugs, now fixed,
220	   worth knowing about if this geometry gets extended:
221	   - The pin height (5 mm) and arm width (2 mm) are far smaller than the
222	     general lambda/N mesh (~19 mm coarse), so nothing bracketed them and
223	     the solver silently dropped the port (`Lumped Element snapping
224	     failed! Dimension is: 0` — *every* primitive logged "Unused"). Fixed
225	     with explicit `mesh.AddLine('z', [..., 0, h, ...])` plus
226	     `metal_edge_res` on every `AddEdges2Grid` call, mirroring the
227	     official tutorial's pattern for resolving sub-wavelength features.
228	   - The arm direction, first derived from an arbitrary feed/short offset,
229	     could point the arm straight off the board into free space for an
230	     edge-placed candidate. Fixed by deriving arm direction from the board
231	     geometry (short pin → board interior) instead.
232	   - The feed pin was offset *perpendicular* to the arm so its top end
233	     never touched the arm conductor — the port drove a stub connected to
234	     nothing (S11 flat at -0.05 dB, VSWR 314, across the whole band: total
235	     reflection, no coupling at all). Fixed by offsetting the feed *along*
236	     the arm axis instead, between the short pin and the open end.
237	   - **Current state after all three fixes:** the port now genuinely
238	     couples into the structure (VSWR dropped from 314 to ~24), but S11 is
239	     still only about -0.7 dB and monotonic across the narrow 1565-1585 MHz
240	     sweep — no resonance dip lands inside the window yet. That's a
241	     **tuning** problem (untuned first-guess dimensions), not a plumbing
242	     bug: nothing in the pipeline is known to be broken, but nothing has
243	     confirmed it's *right* either. Step 2 (tutorial cross-check) and step
244	     4 (PyNEC cross-check) are exactly the two remaining checks that would
245	     tell the difference — do those before trusting a specific resonance
246	     number.
247	4. **Cross-check against PyNEC.** Same IFA geometry (bare PEC, no
248	   dielectrics), same frequency, run through both solvers. Resonance and
249	   input resistance should be in the same ballpark. This is the
250	   openEMS-specific counterpart to step 2 and catches setup mistakes
251	   (units, mesh, port definition) that a lone tutorial re-run wouldn't.
252	   Blocked on the PyNEC/MSVC gap noted above.
253	6. ~~Swap in real materials from the Blender export~~ **Done, bbox-only.**
254	   `geometry._add_device_materials()` reads `device['parts']` (from
255	   `rf/blend_loader/load_blend.py`'s `device.json`) and adds one CSXCAD
256	   `AddMaterial` per distinct `material_key` (epsilon/kappa/mue from
257	   `eps_r`/`sigma_S_per_m`/`mu_r`), with one `AddBox` per part using its
258	   `bbox_mm`. Runs automatically whenever `device['parts']` is
259	   non-empty — no new `SimOptions` flag. Ran end-to-end against the real
260	   Apple iPhone 15 Pro asset (`data/apple_iphone_15_pro/`, 191 parts, 13
261	   material keys, antennas excluded per the asset's own brief) with the
262	   GPS-L1 IFA candidate resized to its real footprint (71.45 x 146.6mm,
263	   computed from the parts' own combined bbox): S11 shifted from -9.8dB
264	   (bare PEC ground plane) to -7.5dB once the real dielectrics/lossy
265	   metal were in the solve — evidence the materials are actually loading
266	   the antenna, not inert. Two things worth knowing:
267	   - **bbox-only, not real mesh shape.** The STLs `load_blend.py` exports
268	     per part aren't imported as polyhedra — 191 `AddPolyhedronReader`
269	     calls (500k+ triangles total) would blow the runtime budget step 7
270	     is meant to protect. Each part becomes one axis-aligned box with
271	     that material's `eps_r`/`sigma_S_per_m`/`mu_r`, coordinate-shifted so
272	     the parts' own bbox starts at `(0, 0, 0)` (a device manifest's
273	     coordinates are Blender-native/centred; the ground plane/antenna use
274	     a corner-anchored `[0, board_w] x [0, board_l]` frame).
275	   - **No collision-awareness.** Nothing checks whether a device part
276	     (e.g. the battery, the titanium frame) overlaps the antenna's own
277	     geometry at the chosen `candidate.position_mm` — that's on
278	     placement/`candidate.keepout_mm`, not this function. Also hit and
279	     fixed along the way: `load_blend.py` assumed the axe fixture's
280	     schema (`material_vocabulary_used` + a `parts` list) and silently
281	     returned `eps_r=None`/`sigma_S_per_m=None` for all 191 iPhone parts,
282	     whose `materials.json` nests the same fields differently
283	     (`materials: {key: {em_from_vocabulary: {...}}}`, no `parts` list —
284	     identity is name-only). Fixed to check both shapes; the axe fixture
285	     re-verified unaffected.
286	7. **Keep runtime bounded.** Expose `sim.mesh_res` and the band's frequency
287	   window as the two speed knobs (per `deep_research_on_challenge.md`
288	   Stage 2: keep each run under ~5-10 min). The narrowed GPS-L1-only
289	   bandwidth chosen above is exactly this lever applied to band selection.
290	8. **Hand off.** `run_simulation` ships as a pure function + a thin CLI
291	   (`python -m rf.run_simulation config.json`) so the FastAPI teammate can
292	   `import` it directly — no HTTP/server code needed from this workstream.
293

1	# AI Antenna Engineer — backend
2	
3	FastAPI backend that turns Devin into an RF engineer: it reads a phone build
4	file (`.blend`), proposes antenna placements, a solver simulates them,
5	evidence goes back, and the agent iterates until it judges the design good
6	enough. Architecture, contracts and decisions: [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md).
7	
8	## Run
9	
10	```bash
11	uv sync
12	uv run uvicorn app.main:app --port 8000
13	```
14	
15	Live agent needs `.env` (gitignored) with `DEVIN_API_KEY`, `DEVIN_ORG_ID`,
16	optional `DEVIN_MAX_ACU` / `DEVIN_MODE` / `DEVIN_REPO` (`owner/repo`; when
17	set, Devin clones it and uses the `blend-extract` skill — otherwise the
18	extraction script is inlined in the prompt). Without `.env`, pass
19	`"agent": "mock"`.
20	
21	`.blend` extraction needs a **Python 3.11 + `bpy`** interpreter (the backend
22	itself is 3.12). Resolution order: `BPY_PYTHON=<python>`, `BLENDER=<blender>`
23	(headless), else an ephemeral `uv run --python 3.11 --with bpy` (first run
24	downloads ~220 MB). Outputs cache under `var/devices/`.
25	
26	Offline self-test (no Devin, no bpy, ~10 s): `uv run python scripts/selftest.py`
27	
28	No-HTTP smoke tests:
29	
30	```bash
31	uv run python scripts/dev_run.py                                           # canned spec, mock
32	BLEND=../data/phone_synth_v1/phone_synth_v1.blend uv run python scripts/dev_run.py
33	AGENT=devin BLEND=../data/phone_synth_v1/phone_synth_v1.blend uv run python scripts/dev_run.py
34	```
35	
36	Assets: the real iPhone 15 Pro `.blend` + `materials.json` lives on branch
37	`feat/simulation` under `data/apple_iphone_15_pro/` (verified end to end);
38	`data/phone_synth_v1/` is a synthetic 15-part fixture, regenerable with
39	`uv run --no-project --python 3.11 --with bpy python ../tools/make_phone_blend.py --out ../data/phone_synth_v1`.
40	
41	## API
42	
43	| Method | Path | Notes |
44	|---|---|---|
45	| POST | `/devices` | multipart `blend` (+ optional `materials` sidecar, `wait=true`) → `{device_id, status, spec, anchors, ambiguities, size_mm, frame, artifacts}` |
46	| GET | `/devices/{id}` | same snapshot (poll when `wait=false`) |
47	| GET | `/devices/{id}/artifacts/{name}` | `device.glb` (viewer, canonical frame), `geometry.json`, `materials.json`, `parts/<node>.stl` |
48	| POST | `/runs` | `{"device_id"?: str, "prompt": str, "bands": ["wifi24"], "agent": "devin"\|"mock", "extract"?: "agent"\|"backend"}` → `{run_id}`; no `device_id` ⇒ canned spec |
49	| GET | `/runs` | list runs |
50	| GET | `/runs/{id}` | snapshot: status, stage, spec, anchors, spec_source, ambiguities, candidates, results, final (incl. `agent_report`), artifacts |
51	| POST | `/runs/{id}/messages` | `{"text": str}` — mid-run user feedback; delivered with the agent's next evidence message, echoed as `agent_message{role: user}` |
52	| GET | `/runs/{id}/artifacts/{name}` | `report.md`, `run.json`, `s11_<candidate_id>.csv` |
53	| WS | `/runs/{id}/events?since=N` | event stream; replays everything after seq N on (re)connect |
54	| GET | `/healthz` | liveness |
55	
56	Bands: `lte_low gps_l1 wifi24 n78 wifi5` (mirror of the frontend catalogue).
57	
58	Event envelope: `{run_id, seq, ts, stage, type, payload}` with `type` one of
59	`stage_started stage_progress agent_message candidates_proposed sim_started
60	sim_result iteration_scored decision artifact run_finished error`.
61	Stages: `extract` (agent reads the build file; `decision{spec accepted,
62	crosscheck, overrides}`), `spec` (`artifact{name: device_spec, spec, anchors,
63	ambiguities, source}`), `agent_loop`, `report` (`run_finished{ranking, best,
64	best_candidate, rationale, truncated}` then `artifact{name: agent_report}` and
65	`artifact{name: report.md, url}` as addenda). `sim_result` payload is a
66	`SimResult`; `iteration_scored` carries the full evidence report
67	(diffs/trend/hints) the agent reasons over.
68	
69	## Seams
70	
71	- **Agent**: `app/agent/port.py` — Devin (`app/agent/devin.py`, default) or
72	  the offline mock. The orchestrator owns the workflow either way.
73	- **Simulation**: one callable, `solve(spec, band, candidate) -> SimResult`,
74	  selected with `SIM_SOLVER=module:function` (default: bundled reference
75	  oracle `app.sim.oracle:solve`). **Sim team:** your `rf.run_simulation(config)`
76	  is already wired — start the backend with
77	  `SIM_SOLVER=app.sim.rf_adapter:solve` (optional `SIM_OPTS='{"mesh_res":
78	  "coarse","freq_points":21}'`, `MAX_BATCH=8` to cap candidates per agent
79	  turn); `app/sim/rf_adapter.py` is the only file that knows your
80	  config/result shape. `config.device.manifest_path` points at the
81	  device's `geometry.json` (your `device.json` manifest shape, plus
82	  `parts/*.stl`); `spec.components[].role == "ground"` names the reference
83	  plane. Expect minutes per solve with FDTD — batch sizes in the agent
84	  protocol should shrink accordingly.
85	- **Geometry**: `tools/extract_blend.py` is the single extraction script
86	  (Devin and backend run the identical file); `app/geometry/classify.py` is
87	  the single place a `DeviceSpec` is assembled (heuristics + agent overrides).
88	- **Frontend**: `DeviceSpec`/`Anchor`/`Candidate`/`SimResult` mirror
89	  `frontend/src/lib/types.ts`; additive optional fields only (`role`,
90	  `em_source`, `region_pref`, `color`). The glb's node names equal
91	  `components[].name` and its coordinates equal `bbox_mm` (mm, no Y-up flip).

1	"""Adapter from our solver seam to the sim workstream's entry point.
2	
3	Their contract (rf/run_simulation.py, branch feat/simulation):
4	
5	    run_simulation(config: dict) -> dict          # SimResult-shaped
6	    config = {"candidate": {...}, "band": {...}, "device": {...}, "sim": {...}}
7	
8	Select it with  SIM_SOLVER=app.sim.rf_adapter:solve . Nothing else in the
9	backend changes: this module runs inside the process pool like any solver.
10	
11	Mapping notes (keep in sync with rf/models.py):
12	- their Candidate dataclass rejects unknown keys -> only the types.ts fields
13	  are forwarded (anchor_id / band_id / prior / rationale / params stay here).
14	- their IFA builder reads the pin height from feed_point_mm.z (0 -> default),
15	  so our `params.height_mm` is mapped onto it.
16	- `device.manifest_path` -> the device's geometry.json (same manifest shape
17	  their blend_loader writes: parts[].{node_path, material_key, eps_r,
18	  sigma_S_per_m, bbox_mm, stl_path}); `device.board.size_mm` is the device
19	  outline; `device.components` is our classified list for when their step 6
20	  (real materials) lands.
21	- their result has no input impedance -> ours stays (0, 0) and the scorer
22	  skips the impedance hints.
23	- `SIM_OPTS` env (JSON) passes solver knobs, e.g.
24	  {"mesh_res": "coarse", "boundary": "MUR", "freq_points": 21}.
25	"""
26	from __future__ import annotations
27	
28	import json
29	import os
30	import sys
31	import time
32	from pathlib import Path
33	
34	from app.models import BandRequirement, Candidate, DeviceSpec, S11Point, SimResult
35	
36	REPO_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
37	
38	
39	def build_config(spec: DeviceSpec, band: BandRequirement, cand: Candidate) -> dict:
40	    feed = list(cand.feed_point_mm)
41	    if "height_mm" in cand.params:
42	        feed[2] = float(cand.params["height_mm"])
43	    device: dict = {
44	        "device_id": spec.device_id,
45	        "name": spec.name,
46	        "board": {"size_mm": list(spec.board.size_mm), "stackup": spec.board.stackup,
47	                  "epsilon_r": spec.board.epsilon_r,
48	                  "loss_tangent": spec.board.loss_tangent},
49	        "enclosure": spec.enclosure.model_dump(),
50	        "components": [c.model_dump() for c in spec.components],
51	    }
52	    if spec.geometry_path:
53	        device["manifest_path"] = spec.geometry_path
54	    return {
55	        "candidate": {
56	            "candidate_id": cand.candidate_id,
57	            "antenna_type": cand.antenna_type,
58	            "position_mm": list(cand.position_mm),
59	            "feed_point_mm": feed,
60	            "length_mm": cand.length_mm,
61	            "orientation": cand.orientation,
62	        },
63	        "band": {
64	            "id": band.id, "f_low_ghz": band.f_low_ghz, "f_high_ghz": band.f_high_ghz,
65	            "s11_db_max": band.s11_db_max, "efficiency_min": band.efficiency_min,
66	        },
67	        "device": device,
68	        "sim": json.loads(os.environ.get("SIM_OPTS", "{}")),
69	    }
70	
71	
72	def from_result(cand: Candidate, out: dict, t0: float) -> SimResult:
73	    curve = [S11Point(f_ghz=round(float(p["f_ghz"]), 4), s11_db=round(float(p["s11_db"]), 2))
74	             for p in out.get("s11_curve", [])]
75	    return SimResult(
76	        candidate_id=cand.candidate_id,
77	        status=out.get("status", "failed"),
78	        runtime_s=round(float(out.get("runtime_s") or (time.perf_counter() - t0)), 3),
79	        s11_curve=curve,
80	        s11_min_db=round(float(out.get("s11_min_db", 0.0)), 2),
81	        resonant_ghz=round(float(out.get("resonant_ghz", 0.0)), 4),
82	        bandwidth_mhz=round(float(out.get("bandwidth_mhz", 0.0)), 1),
83	        efficiency=round(float(out.get("efficiency", 0.0)), 3),
84	        peak_gain_dbi=round(float(out.get("peak_gain_dbi", 0.0)), 2),
85	        vswr=round(min(float(out.get("vswr") or 99.0), 99.0), 2),
86	        impedance_ohm=tuple(out.get("impedance_ohm", (0.0, 0.0))),
87	        meets_requirements=bool(out.get("meets_requirements", False)),
88	        notes=f"[rf.run_simulation] {out.get('notes', '')}",
89	    )
90	
91	
92	def solve(spec: DeviceSpec, band: BandRequirement, cand: Candidate) -> SimResult:
93	    t0 = time.perf_counter()
94	    if str(REPO_DIR) not in sys.path:
95	        sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_DIR))
96	    try:
97	        from rf.run_simulation import run_simulation  # sim workstream, repo root
98	    except Exception as e:
99	        return SimResult(candidate_id=cand.candidate_id, status="failed",
100	                         runtime_s=round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 3),
101	                         notes=f"rf.run_simulation not importable: {e}")
102	    try:
103	        out = run_simulation(build_config(spec, band, cand))
104	        return from_result(cand, out, t0)
105	    except Exception as e:  # their builder raises ImportError without openEMS
106	        return SimResult(candidate_id=cand.candidate_id, status="failed",
107	                         runtime_s=round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 3),
108	                         notes=f"rf.run_simulation error: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")

1	"""Devin v3 adapter behind AgentPort (DESIGN.md §3-4).
2	
3	Maps our synchronous request/response seam onto Devin's async session:
4	one long-lived session per run; `next_action` sends the evidence message and
5	polls the message stream until a fenced ```json action block appears. The
6	orchestrator — not Devin — stays in control of the workflow; Devin is one
7	opaque reasoning node.
8	
9	Env: DEVIN_API_KEY (cog_...), DEVIN_ORG_ID. Optional: DEVIN_BASE_URL,
10	DEVIN_MAX_ACU, DEVIN_MODE, DEVIN_POLL_S."""
11	from __future__ import annotations
12	
13	import asyncio
14	import json
15	import os
16	import re
17	import time
18	from pathlib import Path
19	
20	import httpx
21	from pydantic import TypeAdapter, ValidationError
22	
23	from app.agent import prompts
24	from app.agent.port import RunContext
25	from app.models import AgentRequest, DoneRequest, IterationReport
26	
27	_ACTION = TypeAdapter(AgentRequest)
28	_FENCE = re.compile(r"```json\s*(.*?)```", re.DOTALL)
29	
30	MAX_PROTOCOL_RETRIES = 2
31	MIN_MESSAGE_SPACING_S = 30.0  # documented per-session message rate limit
32	
33	
34	class DevinConfigError(RuntimeError):
35	    pass
36	
37	
38	class DevinAgent:
39	    def __init__(self) -> None:
40	        key = os.environ.get("DEVIN_API_KEY")
41	        org = os.environ.get("DEVIN_ORG_ID")
42	        if not key or not org:
43	            raise DevinConfigError("DEVIN_API_KEY and DEVIN_ORG_ID are required")
44	        base = os.environ.get("DEVIN_BASE_URL", "https://api.devin.ai")
45	        self._org_base = f"{base}/v3/organizations/{org}"
46	        self._http = httpx.AsyncClient(
47	            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}"}, timeout=60.0)
48	        self.poll_s = float(os.environ.get("DEVIN_POLL_S", "10"))
49	        self.session_id: str | None = None
50	        self._cursor: str | None = None
51	        self._seen: set[str] = set()  # processed message ids: end_cursor is
52	        # INCLUSIVE of the last item, so cursor-only polling re-delivers the
53	        # final message of each page — dedupe is mandatory (found live 2026-08-22)
54	        self._narration: list[str] = []
55	        self._last_send = 0.0
56	        self._session_url: str | None = None
57	
58	    # ------------------------------------------------------------ AgentPort --
59	
60	    async def start(self, ctx: RunContext) -> None:
61	        repo = os.environ.get("DEVIN_REPO") or None
62	        body = {
63	            "title": f"antenna-run {ctx.run_id}",
64	            "tags": ["antenna", ctx.run_id],
65	            "structured_output_schema": prompts.STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_SCHEMA,
66	            "structured_output_required": False,
67	        }
68	        if ctx.extract_mode == "agent" and ctx.blend_path:
69	            urls = [await self._upload(ctx.blend_path)]
70	            if ctx.sidecar_path:
71	                urls.append(await self._upload(ctx.sidecar_path))
72	            body["attachment_urls"] = urls
73	            # private repo + no GitHub integration -> inline the script instead
74	            body["prompt"] = prompts.extraction_prompt(
75	                ctx, repo, None if repo else prompts.script_source())
76	            self._narration.append(
77	                f"Uploaded {ctx.blend_path.name} to the session; the agent reads "
78	                f"the build file itself ({'repo skill' if repo else 'inlined script'}).")
79	        else:
80	            body["prompt"] = prompts.initial_prompt(ctx)
81	        if os.environ.get("DEVIN_MAX_ACU"):
82	            body["max_acu_limit"] = int(os.environ["DEVIN_MAX_ACU"])
83	        if os.environ.get("DEVIN_MODE"):
84	            body["devin_mode"] = os.environ["DEVIN_MODE"]
85	        if repo:
86	            body["repos"] = [repo]
87	        r = await self._request("POST", f"{self._org_base}/sessions", json=body)
88	        data = r.json()
89	        self.session_id = data["session_id"]
90	        self._session_url = data.get("url")
91	        self._last_send = time.monotonic()
92	        self._narration.append(
93	            f"Devin session started: {self._session_url or self.session_id}")
94	
95	    async def brief(self, ctx: RunContext) -> None:
96	        await self._send(prompts.brief_message(ctx, ctx.meta.get("crosscheck", "")))
97	
98	    async def _upload(self, path: Path) -> str:
99	        """POST /attachments (multipart `file`) -> pre-signed URL for
100	        `attachment_urls` (v3 docs, verified 2026-08-22)."""
101	        with path.open("rb") as f:
102	            r = await self._request(
103	                "POST", f"{self._org_base}/attachments",
104	                files={"file": (path.name, f, "application/octet-stream")},
105	                timeout=600.0)
106	        return r.json()["url"]
107	
108	    async def next_action(self, report: IterationReport | None) -> AgentRequest:
109	        if report is not None:
110	            await self._send(prompts.report_message(report))
111	        for attempt in range(MAX_PROTOCOL_RETRIES + 1):
112	            action, err = await self._await_action()
113	            if action is not None:
114	                return action
115	            if attempt < MAX_PROTOCOL_RETRIES:
116	                await self._send(
117	                    f"Your last reply had no valid action ({err}). Reply with "
118	                    f"exactly one fenced ```json block per the protocol.")
119	        raise RuntimeError(f"agent protocol failure after retries: {err}")
120	
121	    async def narrate(self) -> list[str]:
122	        out, self._narration = self._narration, []
123	        return out
124	
125	    async def close(self, reason: str) -> dict | None:
126	        """Closing message, then wait briefly for Devin's structured_output
127	        (it updates on Devin's schedule; ~30-60 s after the done action in
128	        practice). The session is left alive for inspection in the Devin UI
129	        unless DEVIN_TERMINATE_ON_CLOSE=1 — an idle session burns no ACUs."""
130	        report = None
131	        try:
132	            if self.session_id:
133	                await self._send(
134	                    f"Run is being closed ({reason}). Update your structured "
135	                    f"output with final status. No further reply is needed.")
136	                for _ in range(int(os.environ.get("DEVIN_REPORT_POLLS", "6"))):
137	                    r = await self._request(
138	                        "GET", f"{self._org_base}/sessions/{self.session_id}")
139	                    so = r.json().get("structured_output")
140	                    if so and (so.get("status") == "concluded" or so.get("final")):
141	                        report = so
142	                        break
143	                    await asyncio.sleep(self.poll_s)
144	                if os.environ.get("DEVIN_TERMINATE_ON_CLOSE") == "1":
145	                    await self._request(
146	                        "DELETE", f"{self._org_base}/sessions/{self.session_id}")
147	        except Exception as e:
148	            self._narration.append(f"close: {e}")
149	        await self._http.aclose()
150	        return report
151	
152	    # ------------------------------------------------------------- internals --
153	
154	    async def _send(self, message: str) -> None:
155	        wait = MIN_MESSAGE_SPACING_S - (time.monotonic() - self._last_send)
156	        if wait > 0:
157	            await asyncio.sleep(wait)
158	        await self._request(
159	            "POST", f"{self._org_base}/sessions/{self.session_id}/messages",
160	            json={"message": message})
161	        self._last_send = time.monotonic()
162	
163	    async def _await_action(self) -> tuple[AgentRequest | None, str]:
164	        """Poll messages until a devin-sourced message with a parsable action
165	        arrives, narrating everything else. Also watches session status."""
166	        err = "no reply"
167	        while True:
168	            for msg in await self._poll_messages():
169	                text = msg.get("message", "")
170	                action, this_err = self._parse_action(text)
171	                narration = _FENCE.sub("", text).strip()
172	                if narration:
173	                    self._narration.append(narration)
174	                if action is not None:
175	                    return action, ""
176	                if this_err:
177	                    err = this_err
178	            status = await self._status()
179	            if status in ("exit", "error"):
180	                return DoneRequest(
181	                    action="done", ranking=[],
182	                    rationale=f"session ended ({status}) without explicit done"
183	                ), ""
184	            await asyncio.sleep(self.poll_s)
185	
186	    async def _poll_messages(self) -> list[dict]:
187	        params = {"first": 100}
188	        if self._cursor:
189	            params["after"] = self._cursor
190	        r = await self._request(
191	            "GET", f"{self._org_base}/sessions/{self.session_id}/messages",
192	            params=params)
193	        data = r.json()
194	        items = data.get("items", data if isinstance(data, list) else [])
195	        cursor = (data.get("end_cursor") if isinstance(data, dict) else None) or \
196	                 (data.get("page_info", {}).get("end_cursor")
197	                  if isinstance(data, dict) else None)
198	        if cursor:
199	            self._cursor = cursor
200	        fresh = []
201	        for m in items:
202	            mid = str(m.get("event_id") or m.get("id")
203	                      or f"{m.get('created_at')}-{hash(m.get('message',''))}")
204	            if mid in self._seen:
205	                continue
206	            self._seen.add(mid)
207	            if m.get("source") == "devin":
208	                fresh.append(m)
209	        return fresh
210	
211	    async def _status(self) -> str:
212	        r = await self._request(
213	            "GET", f"{self._org_base}/sessions/{self.session_id}")
214	        return r.json().get("status", "running")
215	
216	    def _parse_action(self, text: str) -> tuple[AgentRequest | None, str]:
217	        blocks = _FENCE.findall(text)
218	        err = ""
219	        for raw in reversed(blocks):  # last block wins if several
220	            try:
221	                return _ACTION.validate_python(json.loads(raw)), ""
222	            except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValidationError) as e:
223	                err = str(e)[:300]
224	        return None, err or "no json block found"
225	
226	    async def _request(self, method: str, url: str, **kw) -> httpx.Response:
227	        delay = 2.0
228	        for _ in range(6):
229	            r = await self._http.request(method, url, **kw)
230	            if r.status_code == 429:
231	                retry = float(r.headers.get("Retry-After", delay))
232	                await asyncio.sleep(min(retry, 60.0))
233	                delay = min(delay * 2, 60.0)
234	                continue
235	            if r.status_code >= 400:
236	                raise RuntimeError(
237	                    f"Devin API {r.status_code} on {method} {url.split('/v3/')[-1]}: "
238	                    f"{r.text[:300]}")
239	            return r
240	        raise RuntimeError(f"Devin API rate-limited after retries: {url}")
241

1	"""The run state machine (DESIGN.md §5). This module — not the agent vendor —
2	owns the workflow: it services agent requests, enforces the simulation gate,
3	emits every progress event, and guarantees the run ends with a best-so-far
4	result even when barriers trip.
5	
6	Loop contract: the agent is asked for one action at a time (AgentPort). The
7	only hard rule is the gate — no `done` is accepted for an unsimulated design;
8	the orchestrator simulates it and lets the evidence speak first."""
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	import asyncio
12	import os
13	import time
14	
15	from app.agent.port import AgentPort, RunContext
16	from app.geometry.classify import Override, classify
17	from app.geometry.spec import make_anchors
18	from app.models import (BandRequirement, Candidate, DoneRequest, EventType,
19	                        IterationReport, SimulateRequest, SpecRequest,
20	                        SweepRequest, WriteBuilderRequest)
21	from app.runs.store import Run
22	from app.sim import pool
23	from app.sim.score import build_report
24	
25	MAX_WALL_CLOCK_S = 8 * 60          # crash barrier, not pacing (agent self-paces)
26	# cap per simulate/sweep request: 40 is fine for the ms-per-solve reference
27	# oracle; set MAX_BATCH=8 or so when an FDTD engine (minutes per solve) is wired
28	MAX_BATCH = int(os.environ.get("MAX_BATCH", "40"))
29	# agent-side extraction: pip install bpy (~220 MB) + Blender load + reasoning
30	EXTRACT_TIMEOUT_S = float(os.environ.get("EXTRACT_TIMEOUT_S", "600"))
31	
32	
33	async def drive(run: Run, agent: AgentPort) -> None:
34	    try:
35	        await _drive(run, agent)
36	    except Exception as e:
37	        run.log.emit(run.stage, EventType.error, {"error": str(e)})
38	        ranking = _best_ranking(run)
39	        if ranking:
40	            # never fail empty: agent-channel death degrades to best-so-far
41	            run.truncated = True
42	            await _finish(run, ranking,
43	                          f"agent channel failed ({e}); best simulated design "
44	                          f"returned", agent)
45	            return
46	        if type(agent).__name__ != "MockAgent":
47	            # nothing simulated yet -> the heuristic agent finishes the run
48	            # (DESIGN.md §6.3/§10): the demo always ends with a result
49	            from app.agent.mock import MockAgent
50	            run.log.emit(run.stage, EventType.decision, {
51	                "decision": f"agent channel failed before any simulation ({e}); "
52	                            f"falling back to the built-in heuristic agent"})
53	            run.spec_source += "+mock-fallback"
54	            try:
55	                await agent.close("agent failure — mock fallback")
56	            except Exception:
57	                pass
58	            await drive(run, MockAgent())
59	            return
60	        run.status = "failed"
61	        run.log.emit(run.stage, EventType.run_finished,
62	                     {"status": "failed", "error": str(e)})

64	
65	async def _drive(run: Run, agent: AgentPort) -> None:
66	    device = run.device
67	    # a mock taking over after the spec was accepted must not re-extract
68	    do_extract = (device is not None and run.extract_mode == "agent"
69	                  and run.spec_source.startswith("backend"))
70	    ctx = RunContext(
71	        run_id=run.id, prompt=run.prompt, spec=run.spec, anchors=run.anchors,
72	        band_ids=run.band_ids,
73	        budget_note=f"~{MAX_WALL_CLOCK_S // 60} minutes wall clock for the design "
74	                    f"loop; simulate before concluding; spend it as you judge best.",
75	        extract_mode="agent" if do_extract else "backend",
76	        blend_path=device.blend_path() if device else None,
77	        sidecar_path=device.sidecar_path() if device else None,
78	        geometry=device.geometry if device else None,
79	        ambiguities=list(run.ambiguities))
80	
81	    if do_extract:
82	        # ---- EXTRACT: the agent reads the build file itself (ADR-2) ----
83	        run.stage = "extract"
84	        run.log.emit("extract", EventType.stage_started, {
85	            "stage": "extract", "blend": ctx.blend_path.name if ctx.blend_path else None,
86	            "backend_extraction": {"n_parts": ctx.geometry["n_parts"],
87	                                   "size_mm": ctx.geometry["size_mm"]}})
88	        await agent.start(ctx)
89	        await _narrate(run, agent)
90	        try:
91	            action = await asyncio.wait_for(agent.next_action(None), EXTRACT_TIMEOUT_S)
92	        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
93	            action = None
94	            run.log.emit("extract", EventType.decision, {
95	                "decision": f"agent extraction exceeded {EXTRACT_TIMEOUT_S:.0f}s — "
96	                            f"backend extraction used"})
97	        await _narrate(run, agent)
98	        crosscheck = _accept_spec(run, action)
99	        ctx.spec, ctx.anchors, ctx.ambiguities = run.spec, run.anchors, list(run.ambiguities)
100	        ctx.meta["crosscheck"] = crosscheck
101	        _emit_spec(run)
102	        await agent.brief(ctx)
103	        await _narrate(run, agent)
104	    else:
105	        run.stage = "spec"
106	        run.log.emit("spec", EventType.stage_started, {"stage": "spec"})
107	        _emit_spec(run)
108	        await agent.start(ctx)
109	        await _narrate(run, agent)
110	
111	    run.stage = "agent_loop"
112	    run.log.emit("agent_loop", EventType.stage_started, {"stage": "agent_loop"})
113	    t0 = time.time()
114	
115	    report: IterationReport | None = None
116	    history_best: list[float] = []
117	
118	    while True:
119	        if time.time() - t0 > MAX_WALL_CLOCK_S:
120	            run.truncated = True
121	            run.log.emit("agent_loop", EventType.decision,
122	                         {"decision": "wall-clock barrier tripped"})
123	            await _finish(run, _best_ranking(run),
124	                          "wall-clock barrier: returning best-so-far", agent)
125	            return
126	
127	        report = _with_user_notes(run, report)
128	        action = await agent.next_action(report)
129	        await _narrate(run, agent)
130	
131	        if isinstance(action, SimulateRequest):
132	            cands = action.candidates[:MAX_BATCH]
133	            run.iteration += 1
134	            for c in cands:
135	                run.candidates[c.candidate_id] = c
136	            run.log.emit("agent_loop", EventType.candidates_proposed, {
137	                "iteration": run.iteration,
138	                "candidates": [c.model_dump() for c in cands]})
139	            results = await _simulate_batch(run, cands)
140	            report = _score(run, results, history_best)
141	
142	        elif isinstance(action, SweepRequest):
143	            base = run.candidates.get(action.candidate_id)
144	            if base is None:
145	                report = _protocol_error(
146	                    run, report, f"sweep references unknown candidate "
147	                                 f"{action.candidate_id!r}")
148	                continue
149	            variants: list[Candidate] = []
150	            v = action.start
151	            while v <= action.stop + 1e-9 and len(variants) < MAX_BATCH:
152	                cid = f"{base.candidate_id}__{action.param}={round(v, 2)}"
153	                if action.param == "length_mm":
154	                    c = base.model_copy(update={
155	                        "candidate_id": cid, "length_mm": round(v, 2)})
156	                else:
157	                    c = base.model_copy(update={
158	                        "candidate_id": cid,
159	                        "params": {**base.params, action.param: round(v, 2)}})
160	                variants.append(c)
161	                run.candidates[cid] = c
162	                v += action.step
163	            run.iteration += 1
164	            run.log.emit("agent_loop", EventType.candidates_proposed, {
165	                "iteration": run.iteration, "sweep": action.model_dump(by_alias=True),
166	                "candidates": [c.model_dump() for c in variants]})
167	            results = await _simulate_batch(run, variants)
168	            report = _score(run, results, history_best)
169	
170	        elif isinstance(action, WriteBuilderRequest):
171	            report = _protocol_error(
172	                run, report,
173	                "write_builder is not available yet (M3); use existing builders: "
174	                "IFA, monopole")
175	
176	        elif isinstance(action, SpecRequest):  # late/duplicate spec (e.g. after timeout)
177	            report = _protocol_error(
178	                run, report,
179	                "spec already accepted (backend classification in effect); continue "
180	                "with simulate / sweep / done")
181	
182	        elif isinstance(action, DoneRequest):
183	            ranking = [cid for cid in action.ranking if cid in run.candidates]
184	            if not ranking:
185	                ranking = _best_ranking(run)
186	            # ---- the simulation gate ----
187	            top = ranking[0] if ranking else None
188	            if top and (top not in run.results
189	                        or run.results[top].status != "complete"):
190	                run.log.emit("agent_loop", EventType.decision, {
191	                    "decision": "gate: recommended design has no simulation on "
192	                                "record — simulating before accepting"})
193	                results = await _simulate_batch(run, [run.candidates[top]])
194	                report = _score(run, results, history_best)
195	                continue  # agent sees the evidence and must conclude again
196	            await _finish(run, ranking, action.rationale, agent)
197	            return

200	def _emit_spec(run: Run) -> None:
201	    run.log.emit(run.stage, EventType.artifact, {
202	        "name": "device_spec", "source": run.spec_source,
203	        "spec": run.spec.model_dump(),
204	        "anchors": [a.model_dump() for a in run.anchors],
205	        "ambiguities": run.ambiguities})
206	
207	
208	def _accept_spec(run: Run, action) -> str:
209	    """Merge the agent's `spec` judgment into the backend extraction (facts)
210	    and cross-check the two extractions. Returns the note sent back with the
211	    design brief. Backend classification is the fallback in every branch —
212	    never block a run on the agent's reading of the file."""
213	    device = run.device
214	    assert device is not None and device.geometry is not None
215	    base = classify(device.geometry, run.band_ids)
216	    if not isinstance(action, SpecRequest):
217	        run.spec_source = "agent+backend-fallback"
218	        note = ("No `spec` action received from the agent; backend extraction + "
219	                "heuristic classification are in effect.")
220	        run.log.emit("extract", EventType.decision, {"decision": note})
221	        return note
222	
223	    ov = {c.name: Override(em=c.em, role=c.role, epsilon_r=c.epsilon_r, note=c.note)
224	          for c in action.components}
225	    merged = classify(device.geometry, run.band_ids, ov, action.ground,
226	                      geometry_path=str(device.dir / "out" / "geometry.json"))
227	    run.spec, run.anchors, run.ambiguities = merged.spec, make_anchors(merged.spec), merged.ambiguities
228	    run.spec_source = "agent"
229	
230	    lines = []
231	    ext = action.extracted or {}
232	    method = ext.get("method", "unknown")
233	    if method == "failed":
234	        lines.append("Your extraction failed; the backend ran the same script "
235	                     "successfully — its geometry is used, your classification "
236	                     "overrides applied where names matched.")
237	    else:
238	        ours = device.geometry
239	        size_ok = n_ok = None
240	        if isinstance(ext.get("size_mm"), list) and len(ext["size_mm"]) == 3:
241	            size_ok = all(abs(float(a) - b) <= 0.02 * max(b, 1.0)
242	                          for a, b in zip(ext["size_mm"], ours["size_mm"]))
243	        if isinstance(ext.get("n_parts"), int):
244	            n_ok = ext["n_parts"] == ours["n_parts"]
245	        if size_ok and n_ok is not False:
246	            lines.append(f"Cross-check: your extraction ({method}) agrees with the "
247	                         f"backend's ({ours['n_parts']} parts, {ours['size_mm']} mm).")
248	        elif size_ok is None and n_ok is None:
249	            lines.append("Cross-check: no size/part count reported; backend geometry used.")
250	        else:
251	            lines.append(f"Cross-check MISMATCH: you reported size {ext.get('size_mm')} / "
252	                         f"{ext.get('n_parts')} parts, backend has {ours['size_mm']} / "
253	                         f"{ours['n_parts']}. Backend geometry is authoritative; "
254	                         f"flag it if you disagree.")
255	    changed = []
256	    by_name = {c.name: c for c in base.spec.components}
257	    for c in merged.spec.components:
258	        b = by_name.get(c.name)
259	        if b and (b.em != c.em or b.role != c.role or b.epsilon_r != c.epsilon_r):
260	            changed.append(f"{c.name}: {b.em}/{b.role} -> {c.em}/{c.role}")
261	    if action.ground and action.ground != next(
262	            c.name for c in base.spec.components if c.role == "ground"):
263	        changed.append(f"ground reference -> {action.ground}")
264	    lines.append(f"Applied {len(changed)} classification override(s)"
265	                 + (": " + "; ".join(changed) if changed else "."))
266	    note = " ".join(lines)
267	    run.log.emit("extract", EventType.decision, {
268	        "decision": "spec accepted", "crosscheck": note, "overrides": changed,
269	        "agent_summary": action.summary, "extracted": ext})
270	    return note
271	
272	
273	def band_for(run: Run, cand: Candidate) -> BandRequirement:
274	    """Each candidate is simulated against its own band (multi-band runs);
275	    unknown band_id falls back to the run's first band."""
276	    bands = {b.id: b for b in run.spec.requirements.bands}
277	    if cand.band_id in bands and cand.band_id in run.band_ids:
278	        return bands[cand.band_id]
279	    return next(b for b in run.spec.requirements.bands if b.id in run.band_ids)
280	
281	
282	def _with_user_notes(run: Run, report: IterationReport | None) -> IterationReport | None:
283	    """Mid-run user feedback (POST /runs/{id}/messages) rides along with the
284	    next evidence message — no extra agent turn, no rate-limit exposure."""
285	    if not run.inbox:
286	        return report
287	    notes = [f"NOTE FROM THE USER: {t}" for t in run.inbox]
288	    run.inbox.clear()
289	    if report is None:
290	        return IterationReport(iteration=run.iteration, reports=[], best_so_far=None,
291	                               trend="first_iteration", notes=notes)
292	    return report.model_copy(update={"notes": [*report.notes, *notes]})
293	
294	
295	async def _simulate_batch(run: Run, cands: list[Candidate]):
296	    results = {}
297	    async def one(c: Candidate):
298	        run.log.emit("agent_loop", EventType.sim_started,
299	                     {"candidate_id": c.candidate_id, "band_id": c.band_id})
300	        r = await pool.solve_async(run.spec, band_for(run, c), c)
301	        run.results[c.candidate_id] = r
302	        results[c.candidate_id] = r
303	        run.log.emit("agent_loop", EventType.sim_result, r.model_dump())
304	    await asyncio.gather(*(one(c) for c in cands))
305	    return results
306	
307	
308	def _score(run: Run, results, history_best: list[float]) -> IterationReport:
309	    report = build_report(run.spec, lambda c: band_for(run, c), run.iteration,
310	                          run.candidates, results, history_best)
311	    if report.reports:
312	        history_best.append(report.reports[0].score)
313	    run.reports.append(report)
314	    run.log.emit("agent_loop", EventType.iteration_scored, report.model_dump())
315	    return report
316	
317	
318	def _protocol_error(run: Run, report: IterationReport | None,
319	                    msg: str) -> IterationReport | None:
320	    run.log.emit("agent_loop", EventType.error, {"protocol": msg})
321	    if report is not None:
322	        return report.model_copy(update={"notes": [*report.notes, msg]})
323	    return IterationReport(iteration=run.iteration, reports=[],
324	                           best_so_far=None, trend="first_iteration",
325	                           notes=[msg])
326	
327	
328	def _best_ranking(run: Run) -> list[str]:
329	    done = [(cid, r) for cid, r in run.results.items() if r.status == "complete"]
330	    done.sort(key=lambda t: t[1].s11_min_db)
331	    return [cid for cid, _ in done[:5]]
332	
333	
334	async def _finish(run: Run, ranking: list[str], rationale: str,
335	                  agent: AgentPort) -> None:
336	    run.stage = "report"
337	    best = ranking[0] if ranking else None
338	    payload = {
339	        "ranking": ranking,
340	        "rationale": rationale,
341	        "truncated": run.truncated,
342	        "best": run.results[best].model_dump() if best else None,
343	        "best_candidate": run.candidates[best].model_dump() if best else None,
344	        "iterations": run.iteration,
345	        "total_sims": len(run.results),
346	        "spec_source": run.spec_source,
347	    }
348	    run.final = payload
349	    run.status = "finished"
350	    run.finished_at = time.time()
351	    run.log.emit("report", EventType.decision,
352	                 {"decision": "accepted", "rationale": rationale})
353	    run.log.emit("report", EventType.run_finished, payload)
354	    # the agent's own structured report arrives on its schedule; it is an
355	    # addendum artifact, never a gate on run_finished
356	    try:
357	        agent_report = await agent.close("finished")
358	    except Exception as e:
359	        agent_report = None
360	        run.log.emit("report", EventType.error, {"error": f"agent close: {e}"})
361	    if agent_report:
362	        run.final["agent_report"] = agent_report
363	        run.log.emit("report", EventType.artifact,
364	                     {"name": "agent_report", "report": agent_report})
365	    run.log.emit("report", EventType.artifact, {
366	        "name": "report.md", "url": f"/runs/{run.id}/artifacts/report.md"})
367	
368	
369	async def _narrate(run: Run, agent: AgentPort) -> None:
370	    for line in await agent.narrate():
371	        run.log.emit(run.stage, EventType.agent_message,
372	                     {"role": "agent", "text": line})

1	"""Backend runner for the SHARED extraction script (tools/extract_blend.py).
2	
3	The same file Devin executes in its VM runs here in a subprocess with a
4	bpy-capable interpreter — demo insurance and the source of the viewer glb.
5	bpy needs Python 3.11 while the backend is 3.12, so the interpreter is
6	resolved, in order:
7	
8	  BPY_PYTHON=/path/to/python   (a venv that has `bpy`)
9	  BLENDER=/path/to/blender     (headless `blender -b --python`)
10	  uv run --no-project --python 3.11 --with bpy   (ephemeral; first run downloads ~220 MB)
11	
12	Outputs land in var/devices/<device_id>/ (geometry.json, device.glb,
13	parts/*.stl) and are reused when the .blend hash matches."""
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	import asyncio
17	import hashlib
18	import json
19	import os
20	import shutil
21	import subprocess
22	from pathlib import Path
23	
24	BACKEND_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
25	REPO_DIR = BACKEND_DIR.parent
26	SCRIPT = REPO_DIR / "tools" / "extract_blend.py"
27	VAR_DIR = Path(os.environ.get("DEVICES_DIR", BACKEND_DIR / "var" / "devices"))
28	
29	
30	class ExtractError(RuntimeError):
31	    pass
32	
33	
34	def device_id_for(blend: Path) -> str:
35	    h = hashlib.sha256()
36	    with blend.open("rb") as f:
37	        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
38	            h.update(chunk)
39	    return f"dev_{h.hexdigest()[:10]}"
40	
41	
42	def _command(args: list[str]) -> list[str]:
43	    if py := os.environ.get("BPY_PYTHON"):
44	        return [py, str(SCRIPT), *args]
45	    if bl := os.environ.get("BLENDER"):

51	def ingest(blend_src: Path, sidecar_src: Path | None, device_id: str | None = None) -> Path:
52	    """Copy the upload into its device dir (the script wants the sidecar next
53	    to the .blend, named materials.json). Returns the device dir."""
54	    device_id = device_id or device_id_for(blend_src)
55	    d = VAR_DIR / device_id

59	        shutil.copyfile(blend_src, dst)

61	        side = d / "materials.json"
62	        if side.resolve() != sidecar_src.resolve():
63	            shutil.copyfile(sidecar_src, side)

67	def extract_sync(device_dir: Path, timeout_s: float | None = None) -> dict:
68	    blend = next(device_dir.glob("*.blend"), None)
69	    if blend is None:
70	        raise ExtractError(f"no .blend in {device_dir}")
71	    out = device_dir / "out"
72	    cached = out / "geometry.json"
73	    if cached.exists():
74	        try:
75	            g = json.loads(cached.read_text())
76	            if g.get("source_sha256") == hashlib.sha256(blend.read_bytes()).hexdigest():
77	                return g
78	        except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
79	            pass
80	    args = [str(blend), "--out", str(out)]
81	    side = device_dir / "materials.json"
82	    if side.exists():
83	        args += ["--materials", str(side)]
84	    timeout_s = timeout_s or float(os.environ.get("EXTRACT_TIMEOUT_S", "900"))
85	    try:
86	        proc = subprocess.run(_command(args), capture_output=True, text=True,
87	                              timeout=timeout_s, cwd=str(REPO_DIR))
88	    except FileNotFoundError as e:
89	        raise ExtractError(f"extraction interpreter not found: {e}") from e
90	    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
91	        raise ExtractError(f"extraction timed out after {timeout_s:.0f}s") from e
92	    if proc.returncode != 0 or not cached.exists():
93	        tail = "\n".join(proc.stderr.strip().splitlines()[-12:])
94	        raise ExtractError(f"extract_blend.py failed (rc={proc.returncode}):\n{tail}")
95	    return json.loads(cached.read_text())
96	
97	
98	async def extract(device_dir: Path) -> dict:
99	    return await asyncio.to_thread(extract_sync, device_dir)

103	    """Resolve a public artifact name to a file inside the device dir."""
104	    out = device_dir / "out"
105	    candidates = {
106	        "geometry.json": out / "geometry.json",
107	        "device.glb": out / "device.glb",
108	        "materials.json": device_dir / "materials.json",
109	    }

112	        p = (out / name).resolve()
113	        if out.resolve() not in p.parents:
114	            return None
115	    return p if p and p.exists() else None

# Wiring Devin (backend) to the real RF simulation — integration plan

> Draft for review, 2026-08-22. Nothing here is implemented yet; this is the
> plan to review before code changes start. Once approved, execute §5 in
> order and check items off in place.

## 1. Where things actually stand

Both sides are individually done, but never run **together for real**:

- `rf/run_simulation(config: dict) -> dict` runs a genuine openEMS FDTD solve
  (IFA-over-ground-plane, optional real device dielectrics via
  `device.manifest_path`). Verified end-to-end on a demo candidate and on the
  real iPhone 15 Pro asset (bbox-approximated materials). **Not yet**
  cross-checked against a known-good resonance (tutorial / PyNEC oracle) —
  see `rf/progress_simulation.md` steps 2 and 4.
- The backend already has an adapter for it: `backend/app/sim/rf_adapter.py`
  maps backend `Candidate`/`DeviceSpec`/`BandRequirement` → rf's config dict
  and rf's result dict → backend `SimResult`. Selecting it is one env var:
  `SIM_SOLVER=app.sim.rf_adapter:solve`.
- `backend/scripts/selftest.py::test_rf_adapter` only exercises this against
  a **stubbed** `rf.run_simulation` (a lambda injected into `sys.modules`).
  The adapter has never actually called the real openEMS solver.

So "connect the agent to the simulation" is really: **make the already-written
adapter work against the real solver**, not build a new integration from
scratch. The gap is narrower than it looks, but it's a real one (§2).

## 2. The actual blocker: two incompatible Python environments

- The backend runs on **Python 3.12** (`backend/pyproject.toml`,
  `requires-python = ">=3.12"`), managed by `uv`.
- openEMS/CSXCAD are prebuilt **Windows wheels for Python 3.11**, installed
  only inside `rf/.venv` (see `rf/README.md` Setup). They are not, and
  cannot be, installed into the backend's own venv (ABI mismatch).
- `rf_adapter.solve()` today does this **in-process**:
  ```python
  sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_DIR))
  from rf.run_simulation import run_simulation   # imports openEMS transitively
  ```
- `app/sim/pool.py` runs `solve()` inside a `ProcessPoolExecutor` — but those
  worker processes are spawned from **the same interpreter as the backend**
  (Python 3.12, no openEMS). The import will fail with `ModuleNotFoundError`
  the moment `SIM_SOLVER=app.sim.rf_adapter:solve` is set on a normal
  `uv run uvicorn ...` backend.

This is the *same* problem the backend already solved once, for `bpy`
(Blender's Python API, also version-pinned): `app/geometry/extract.py`
resolves a separate interpreter (`BPY_PYTHON` / `BLENDER` / ephemeral
`uv run --with bpy`) and shells out via `subprocess.run`, rather than
importing `bpy` in-process. `rf_adapter` needs the same treatment.

## 3. Backend structure, oriented at this integration

```
backend/app/
├── main.py               FastAPI app; lifespan starts/stops the sim process pool
├── api/routes.py          HTTP/WS surface: /runs, /devices, /runs/{id}/events
├── models.py              Pydantic mirror of frontend/src/lib/types.ts —
│                          DeviceSpec, Candidate, SimResult, the agent wire
│                          protocol (SimulateRequest/SweepRequest/DoneRequest/
│                          SpecRequest = AgentRequest union)
├── agent/
│   ├── port.py            AgentPort protocol — the ONE seam between the
│   │                      orchestrator and any agent implementation
│   ├── devin.py           Devin v3 client implementing AgentPort (see §4)
│   ├── mock.py            heuristic drop-in implementing the same protocol
│   └── prompts.py         builds the create-session prompt + per-iteration
│                          evidence messages; defines the fenced-JSON protocol
│                          text Devin is told to follow
├── runs/
│   ├── orchestrator.py    the state machine — THE file that drives a run:
│   │                      services one agent action at a time, enforces the
│   │                      "no unsimulated done" gate, emits every event
│   ├── devices.py         .blend ingest → extraction → DeviceSpec lifecycle
│   ├── events.py, store.py  append-only per-run event log; in-memory registries
│   └── report.py          renders report.md / run.json / S11 CSV artifacts
├── geometry/
│   ├── extract.py         subprocess dispatch to a bpy-capable interpreter
│   │                      (THE PATTERN §5 reuses for rf)
│   ├── classify.py        geometry.json → DeviceSpec (EmClass, roles, ground)
│   ├── spec.py            canned phone_v1 + anchor generation
│   └── bands.py           band catalogue (mirrors frontend/src/lib/device.ts)
└── sim/
    ├── pool.py             ProcessPoolExecutor wrapper; resolves SIM_SOLVER
    │                       and calls `solve(spec, band, cand) -> SimResult`
    ├── oracle.py            bundled reference solver (PyNEC MoM) — default
    ├── rf_adapter.py         <-- what this plan changes; maps to rf/run_simulation
    ├── builders/            oracle's own antenna geometry builders (IFA, monopole)
    └── score.py              turns SimResult(s) into the evidence layers
                               (diff/trend/hint) the agent reasons over
```

**The one seam this plan touches:** `solve(spec, band, cand) -> SimResult` in
`app/sim/rf_adapter.py`, selected by `SIM_SOLVER=app.sim.rf_adapter:solve`.
Nothing in `orchestrator.py`, `pool.py`, `score.py`, or the agent layer needs
to change — that's the point of the seam.

## 4. How Devin actually "calls tools" (brief)

Devin does **not** use a function-calling / native tool-use API the way the
Anthropic Messages API does. There is no schema the backend registers with
Devin that Devin then invokes structurally. Instead:

1. The backend creates one Devin **session** per run (`POST /v3/.../sessions`)
   and sends a big **prompt** (`app/agent/prompts.py`) that includes a
   `## Protocol` section written in plain English + example JSON: *"each of
   your replies must contain exactly one fenced ```json block with ONE
   action: simulate | sweep | done | spec"*.
2. Devin runs autonomously **inside its own VM** — its own shell, filesystem,
   package manager. It can `pip install bpy`, run scripts, read an attached
   `.blend` file, and (if `repos: [...]` is set and the org's GitHub
   integration can see the repo) follow **Skills** — `SKILL.md` files under
   `.agents/skills/` that are auto-discovered and inject procedure ("run
   `tools/extract_blend.py` like this"). None of that VM-internal activity
   (shell commands, file edits) is visible to the backend as structured
   events — it's opaque compute happening on Devin's side.
3. The only thing the backend ever sees is **chat messages** Devin posts
   back into the session, fetched by polling
   `GET /sessions/{id}/messages?after={cursor}` every ~10-30 s
   (`DevinAgent._poll_messages` in `app/agent/devin.py`). Devin has no
   webhooks; this is deliberate, documented API design on their side.
4. `DevinAgent._parse_action` takes the **last fenced ```json block** in each
   new Devin-authored message, JSON-decodes it, and validates it against the
   `AgentRequest` Pydantic union in `app/models.py`. **That fenced block is
   the "tool call"** from the orchestrator's point of view — a
   backend-defined wire protocol carried inside ordinary chat text, not a
   native Devin tool-calling mechanism. Malformed JSON gets one corrective
   message ("your last reply had no valid action...") before falling back.
5. `orchestrator.py` executes the parsed action (run FDTD/PyNEC sims in the
   process pool, score them, build the evidence report) and sends the result
   back as the **next** chat message (`prompts.report_message`). Devin reads
   that evidence and replies with its next action. This request/response
   loop repeats until a `done` action passes the simulation gate.
6. Because `AgentPort` (`app/agent/port.py`) is the same narrow interface for
   both `DevinAgent` and the heuristic `MockAgent`, `orchestrator.py` never
   has agent-vendor-specific code in it — it just calls `next_action(report)`
   and gets back one of `SimulateRequest | SweepRequest | DoneRequest |
   SpecRequest`.

In short: **Devin's "tools" are backend concepts described in a prompt, not
API-registered functions** — the fenced-JSON convention *is* the tool-calling
layer, implemented entirely in our parsing code, not Devin's.

## 5. Step-by-step plan

1. **Add a real CLI entrypoint to `rf/`.** `rf/run_simulation.py`'s
   `if __name__ == "__main__":` block currently only runs a hardcoded demo
   config — it does not read a config path from `sys.argv`, despite both
   `rf/README.md` and `progress_simulation.md` step 8 describing
   `python -m rf.run_simulation config.json` as the intended CLI. This needs
   a small addition before anything can shell out to it — either:
   - extend the existing `__main__` block to accept an optional
     `sys.argv[1]` config path (falls back to the demo when absent), or
   - add a tiny separate `rf/cli.py` (stdin JSON in → stdout JSON out, no new
     dependencies) so the demo `__main__` stays untouched.
   Flag this to the sim team — it's their file, one-line-ish change, but
   blocks step 2 until it exists.

2. **Replace the in-process import in `rf_adapter.solve()` with a subprocess
   call**, mirroring `app/geometry/extract.py`'s `_command()` pattern:
   - Resolve the interpreter: `RF_PYTHON` env var override, else default to
     `<repo_root>/rf/.venv/Scripts/python.exe` (this repo is Windows-only for
     the openEMS wheels anyway); error clearly if it doesn't exist.
   - `subprocess.run([rf_python, "-m", "rf.cli"], cwd=repo_root, input=json.dumps(cfg), capture_output=True, timeout=RF_TIMEOUT_S)`
     — `cwd=repo_root` matters, same reason as `rf/README.md`'s "always
     `python -m rf.<module>`, never direct" rule (relative imports need
     package context).
   - Parse stdout as JSON → existing `from_result()` unchanged.
   - Non-zero exit / timeout / missing interpreter → `SimResult(status="failed", notes=...)`,
     same fail-soft pattern already in the file (never crash a candidate's slot).

3. **Re-tune batch size and timeouts for FDTD's actual cost.** PyNEC (today's
   default oracle) solves in milliseconds; openEMS takes **minutes per
   candidate** (`rf/README.md`: "~2 min" for the demo). Two knobs need to
   change together when `SIM_SOLVER=app.sim.rf_adapter:solve`:
   - `MAX_BATCH` (orchestrator.py caps `simulate`/`sweep` batch size) — drop
     from the default 40 to single digits (the backend README already
     suggests `MAX_BATCH=8`).
   - `MAX_WALL_CLOCK_S` in `orchestrator.py` (currently a flat 8-minute crash
     barrier) — at ~2 min/candidate this barrier trips after only ~4
     candidates total across the whole run. Either raise it via an env var
     when running the real solver, or accept a much smaller effective
     iteration budget and say so in the prompt's budget note.
   - Keep `SIM_OPTS='{"mesh_res":"coarse","freq_points":11-21}'` and a
     narrow band (GPS L1's 1565-1585 MHz, not the full multi-constellation
     window) — this is the runtime lever `rf/progress_simulation.md` step 7
     already identifies.

   through `/devices` (real `.blend` ingest), `classify.py` sets
   `DeviceSpec.geometry_path` to `<device_dir>/out/geometry.json`;
   `rf_adapter.build_config()` forwards that as `device.manifest_path`;
   `rf.device.load_device()` reads it as plain JSON (no `bpy`, by design).
   Spot-check that the field names match exactly (`parts[].{node_path,
   material_key, eps_r, sigma_S_per_m, bbox_mm, stl_path}`) — DESIGN.md §8
   already asserts `geometry.json` is a superset of rf's own manifest shape,
   but this has not been run for real yet.

5. **Test in three widening steps, each gated on the previous passing:**
   1. **Adapter-only, real solver, canned spec:**
      `SIM_SOLVER=app.sim.rf_adapter:solve SIM_OPTS='{"mesh_res":"coarse","freq_points":11}' MAX_BATCH=2 uv run python scripts/dev_run.py`
      — no device ingest, just the canned `phone_v1` board. Confirms the
      subprocess call itself works and returns a real (not stubbed) S11
      curve.
   2. **Real device asset:**
      `BLEND=../data/apple_iphone_15_pro/<file>.blend AGENT=mock SIM_SOLVER=app.sim.rf_adapter:solve uv run python scripts/dev_run.py`
      — confirms `manifest_path` → real bbox materials flow through to an
      actual FDTD solve, not just the bare board.
   3. **Live Devin run**, only once 1-2 are green: `AGENT=devin` against the
      same fixtures, watching wall-clock and batch sizing in practice.
   Add an **opt-in** integration test (e.g.
   `backend/scripts/rf_integration_test.py`) that auto-skips when
   `rf/.venv` isn't present, so this never blocks anyone without the
   openEMS setup — the existing `selftest.py` stays stub-only and fast.

6. **Update docs once verified:** `backend/README.md` "Seams" section and
   `rf/README.md` "Status" currently describe this as untested
   ("...against their real solver only once it runs on a shared machine").
   Replace with the actual first real timing/result once §5 passes.

## 6. Open risks to flag explicitly

- **rf's own resonance numbers are not yet validated** (tutorial cross-check
  and PyNEC cross-check are both still open per
  `rf/progress_simulation.md`). Wiring the plumbing correctly does not by
  itself make a live Devin run's conclusions physically trustworthy — that's
  a separate, pre-existing gap in the sim workstream, not something this
  integration fixes.
- **Windows-only.** openEMS's prebuilt wheels are MSVC/`win_amd64`; this
  whole path only works on a Windows machine with `rf/.venv` set up per
  `rf/README.md`. Worth stating plainly in `backend/README.md` as a
  requirement for whoever flips `SIM_SOLVER`.
- **`rf/cli.py` (or the `__main__` change) is the sim team's file** — raise
  it with them rather than unilaterally changing their entrypoint; keeps
  "one code path" ownership clean the same way `tools/extract_blend.py` is
  shared but singly-owned.

## Proposed concrete file changes (for when this plan is approved)

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `rf/cli.py` (new) or `rf/run_simulation.py` | accept a JSON config via stdin/argv, print result JSON to stdout |
| `backend/app/sim/rf_adapter.py` | subprocess dispatch to `RF_PYTHON` instead of in-process import |
| `backend/scripts/rf_integration_test.py` (new) | opt-in real-solver smoke test, skips if `rf/.venv` absent |
| `backend/README.md`, `rf/README.md` | status update once §5 is verified |
| `.env.example` / README env docs | document `RF_PYTHON`, `RF_TIMEOUT_S`, and the `MAX_BATCH`/`MAX_WALL_CLOCK_S` guidance for FDTD mode |
